answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable stake in a vault and earn access only after completing unpredictable, cross-agent tasks whose results are checked by established agents. A fake operator must fund many stakes, solve many tasks, and risk slashing when identities collude or submit inconsistent answers. Honest agents gain reputation gradually, while a coordinated swarm faces a compounding cost spiral; even a sparrow-sized account cannot multiply cheaply.
